nodes.claim: The perfect pattern engine is a learned representation over raw answer/event sequences — the LLM-shaped move — earned above a data-volume crossover it must prove against its own classical factor layer, which is kept permanently as the auditable layer.
nodes.detail: The scout (2026-08-26) grounds both halves, and the adversarial pass forced the condition INTO the claim string — the unconditional form is not what the evidence licenses. For the learned layer: in exactly this domain — user action streams — reformulating recommendation as generative sequential transduction beats the factorization/feature stack at industrial scale, with power-law returns to compute across three orders of magnitude (Zhai et al., HSTU, ICML 2024; abstract-grade figures: up to 65.8% NDCG over baselines, +12.4% online A/B, 1.5T parameters deployed); an independent academic study finds LLM-style scaling laws do transfer to sequential recommendation and pay precisely on the hard regimes — cold start, robustness, long-term preference (Zhang et al., RecSys 2024); and sequence models are proven production user-representations (Kang & McAuley 2018; Pancha et al., PinnerFormer, KDD 2022, whose dense all-action loss significantly reduces the gap between nightly-batch and real-time embeddings — directly the shape InSight's nightly fit would take). For the architecture-family transfer the seed leaned on: the strongest verified case is ESM-2 (Lin et al., Science 2023, citation fetched from the authors' own repo: a masked-LM over amino-acid sequences folds proteins atomically with no alignments, monotone in scale — CASP14 55.4/52.5/51.3 at 15B/3B/700M, repo-table-grade from the authors' fetched README). But the bio evidence also draws the boundary: transcriptome foundation models — where the sequence is a noisy, sparsely-sampled readout of state rather than the causal substrate — repeatedly lose to trivial baselines zero-shot (Kedzierska et al., Genome Biology 2025) and show NO data-scaling law (DenAdel et al., Nature Methods 2026: 400 pretrained models across 6,400 experiments, performance plateaus at a fraction of current corpus sizes; the 2024 bioRxiv preprint of the same study reported 375 models/3,750 experiments — the figure circulating on its preprint-hosting pages). So the licence is conditional: the LLM-shaped move is licensed for behavioral streams by the behavioral-stream evidence itself (HSTU's domain IS action sequences), not by analogy to biology — all of that evidence is industrial-scale, so the crossover clause in the claim is load-bearing, with pat-6 carrying the crossover and pat-7 the audit layer's own standards. Verification grade: journal pages were egress-blocked from this environment; sources are corroborated across independent bibliographic indexes (DBLP, ACM DL, PMLR, Semantic Scholar, publisher/lab pages) and, where possible, authors' own fetched repository citation blocks (ESM-2, Geneformer, scGPT); the Kedzierska and DenAdel abstracts were fetched via Microsoft Research publication pages, which for DenAdel host the PREPRINT — its published-version figures above are index-grade. Quoted figures are abstract/snippet/repo-table-grade as labeled.

nodes.claim: An auditable layer is permanent: every published pattern must be recomputable by a reader from public numbers.
nodes.detail: Whatever the engine (pat-1), the published artifact stays factor-shaped: vectors with n, reproducible from published aggregates, stable under re-runs (deterministic seeds). This is not conservatism about methods — it is the product's honesty contract extended to methodology: a black-box coupling is an assertion, and the app does not assert what cannot be recomputed. The perfect system therefore treats distillation quality (how much of the learned layer survives into the auditable one) as a first-class metric. Product note (verified in code 2026-08-26): the shipped fit already keeps this contract exactly — functions/src/patternsFit.ts is a K=8 streaming factorization with qid-hash-seeded deterministic vectors, published per-question with its basis n, refit reproducibly from its own log. pat-7 now carries the external evidence that the distillation half of this claim is the genuinely open problem.

nodes.claim: Cross-axiom couplings carry level-specific referents — between-person, plus temporal and contemporaneous within-person — that need not agree in magnitude or sign; a level-blind estimator conflates them, so the perfect engine keeps the person-period as its native record and estimates and publishes both levels, matching each published coupling to its level rather than promoting either.
nodes.detail: Raised argued→cited 2026-08-28 — the 2026-08-25 form said couplings 'graduate' from correlation to within-person change, a promotion reading refuted by its own literature; fissioned 2026-09-01 per central's 2026-08-28 question (go-7): the machinery now stands at pat-9 (conflation is an estimator property), pat-10 (native person-period machinery) and pat-11 (the separation is not free), each with its own sources and status — nothing re-argued in the move, every adversarially-forced qualifier traveling with its claim. This node keeps the estimand thesis and the design consequences. THE ESTIMAND THESIS. The two levels are different estimands answering different questions, and the field's recommendation is to match model to question, never to replace one level with the other (Orth et al. 2021: seven cross-lagged models over 10 samples, N 326–8,259 — CLPM and RI-CLPM were the only two models to estimate cleanly in every sample (the others frequently failed to converge), RI-CLPM fit better, CLPM gave more consistent cross-lagged estimates, the models 'test conceptually distinct processes', and the closing recommendation is CLPM for between-person questions, RI-CLPM for within-person ones; abstract-grade). Divergence between levels is documented to the point of sign reversal, not merely possible in principle: in a three-wave adolescent privacy-invasion/secrecy study (n = 244) the between-person and within-person cross-lagged paths run in opposite directions — privacy invasion predicting more secrecy between persons, higher secrecy predicting LOWER subsequent privacy invasion within persons — the authors' own Simpson's-paradox construction, in their abstract (Dietvorst et al. 2018, abstract-grade). The level-divergence backdrop stays the siblings', leaned on by edge and not re-cited: ergodicity and the 2–4x within-person variance excess are tst-7's, the empirical within-vs-between magnitude ordering is bod-5's (meta-analytic, sleep→self-control, its overlapping-CI and sleep-only caveats inherited, not restated stronger; the adjacent diary evidence there is nightly — nights, not the old detail's 'weeks'), and the published rebuttal to Fisher ('ergodicity is sufficient but not necessary') is carried at map-6, whose stricter honesty grade this node follows. DESIGN CONSEQUENCES, this lane's own inferences and marked so: the person-period is the native record because aggregation to the person is lossy and non-invertible — a coupling fitted on person-aggregates cannot be disaggregated afterwards; the audit layer (pat-2) publishes LEVEL-LABELED artifacts — a between-person loading and a within-person coupling are different published objects, with pat-10's three-network decomposition supplying the label set — the engine-side half of map-6's display rule and of tst-6's two-linked-geometries architecture; the published within-person object is the POPULATION-AVERAGE within-person parameter, never a per-person coupling — tst-6's §9 reading forecloses per-person latent publication, so pat-8's person-specific estimands inform the engine's design without ever reaching the published surface; and the boundary is per-pair — a genotype does not vary within a person, so gene-side couplings have no within-person half (map-6's scope note, honored here). Product note, marked as such: the shipped corpus is nearly all T=1 per (person, question) — answers are create-only (D5) with one in-place edit shape (D86) — so within-person identification is today a statement about what the perfect system RECORDS, which is the point: the record-grain requirement cannot be retrofitted onto person-aggregates. The old gen-4 clause (longitudinal phenotype change measurable at app scale) stays this lane's inference from gen-4's cited cohort sizes, not gen-4's own claim.
sources: Orth, Clark, Donnellan & Robins, 'Testing prospective effects in longitudinal research: Comparing seven competing cross-lagged models', Journal of Personality and Social Psychology 120(4):1013–1034 (2021), DOI 10.1037/pspp0000358, PMID 32730068

Dietvorst, Hiemstra, Hillegers & Keijsers, 'Adolescent perceptions of parental privacy invasion and adolescent secrecy: An illustration of Simpson's paradox', Child Development 89(6):2081–2090 (2018), DOI 10.1111/cdev.13002

nodes.claim: Coupling capacity is bounded by the paired population because pairing is what identifies a cross-axiom coupling: two axes never observed jointly on the same people pin their coupling down only to a conditional Fréchet set, and a point needs further structure — the conditional-independence assumption, an exclusion restriction, or a sample holding the two jointly — so the paired count, never larger than either population, buys identification first and precision second, and the perfect engine budgets both explicitly.
nodes.detail: Raised 2026-09-02; the seed's 'intersection n' was complete-case bookkeeping. With X answered by everyone, Y on axis A only, Z on B only, P(X,Y) and P(X,Z) are identified and P(Y,Z|X) is not — only the set of joints with the right conditional margins, the conditional Fréchet bounds Σ_i p_{X=i}·max{0; p_{j|i}+p_{k|i}−1} ≤ p_jk ≤ Σ_i p_{X=i}·min{p_{j|i}; p_{k|i}} (full-text-grade, StatMatch manual). The conditional-independence assumption P(Y,Z,X)=P(Y|X)P(Z|X)P(X) selects one point, and is an assumption, not an estimate (D'Orazio, Di Zio & Scanu 2006; StatMatch comb.samples). Ridder & Moffitt: 'without further assumptions the (conditional) Fréchet bounds ... is all that can be learned' (snippet-grade); Cross & Manski give the sharp identification region for the long regression from two short ones — the unpaired case exactly — shrunk by exclusion restrictions, sometimes to a point (abstract-grade); in a parametric setup ranges 'are the only estimable items' absent restrictive assumptions on the relationship between the non-jointly-observed variables (Conti, Marella & Scanu 2017); Ahfock et al.: partially identified (Manski's frame). This lane's entailment, marked, no source saying it so: at fixed X the set is a functional of population margins, so unpaired respondents shrink sampling error AROUND the bounds, never their width — volume narrows it only by making a finer X estimable. Two nuances: shared covariates narrow without closing (the X-subset most associated with both Y and Z reduces average bound width — StatMatch Fbwidths.by.x; Ridder & Moffitt: bounds 'usually not sufficiently narrow' unless common variables correlate highly with both); and joint observation buys identification — an auxiliary sample holding Y and Z together corrects the CIA table (Renssen 1998, secondary via the StatMatch manual), the split-questionnaire design its constructive version (Raghunathan & Grizzle 1995; Ali & Kauermann 2021) — pat-12's subject. CONSEQUENCES, this lane's, marked. Conserved density stands (db-8). The budget is two ledgers: identification — which axis pairs have ANY joint observation, a pair with none publishing its Fréchet interval under declared X, never a CIA point (pat-2's contract extended to interval and assumption) — and precision, the paired count per pair. The marginal value of one more paired person peaks at zero, a step from set to point; above zero cen-2's 'pairing governs precision, not definition' holds; at zero value is unidentified, not imprecise — a boundary contradiction of cen-2's 'does not zero value', carried to central via the LOG. Verification: full texts egress-blocked except the StatMatch manual; the rest search-index-corroborated, graded per string.

nodes.claim: The perfect engine treats honesty failures as model bugs: selection bias, retest effects and drift are modeled, not footnoted.
nodes.detail: Who answers is never random (interest-selected feeds, attrition), items age (retest and exposure effects), and populations drift. An engine that publishes couplings without modeling these publishes artifacts of its own serving policy. The perfect engine carries an explicit sampling model beside every coupling — which is also what makes the core-served-to-everyone idea a methodological theorem here, not a product preference.

nodes.claim: Below a data-volume crossover the tuned classical baseline beats the learned sequence model — so engine choice is a measurement, and the perfect engine proves its choice against its own factor layer, out of sample, continuously.
nodes.detail: The negative results are as replicated as the positive ones, across two fields. Recommendation: the TOIS 2021 extension found 12 of 26 neural recommenders reproducible, 11 of the 12 beaten by conceptually simpler tuned methods, and with properly tuned linear/MF baselines only one remained clearly better, on one dataset (Ferrari Dacrema et al., TOIS 2021 — abstract-grade counts; the RecSys 2019 Best Long Paper original reported 18 papers / 7 reproducible / 6 outperformed). The mechanism is inductive bias once both sides are properly tuned: a tuned dot product substantially beats a learned MLP similarity, because a universal approximator must spend data LEARNING the prior the factor model gets for free (Rendle et al., RecSys 2020 — tuning is load-bearing in their result). The adjacent tabular domain gives the sharpest threshold: tree models still beat deep learning at ~10K samples, attributed to inductive bias under an explicitly budgeted hyperparameter search (Grinsztajn et al., NeurIPS 2022). And the pro-sequence academic literature itself partly measures compute, not architecture: published BERT4Rec/SASRec comparisons are mutually inconsistent, and the original BERT4Rec results reproduce only with up to 30x the default training budget (Petrov & Macdonald, RecSys 2022). Biology replays the same law where the sequence is a state readout — the evidence here is transcriptomic, note, not genotype-to-trait, so gen-5's own scout question (trait-scale delivery vs a polygenic-score baseline) remains open: L1 logistic regression shows no significant difference from scBERT on cell-type annotation even with small training data (Boiarsky et al., Nat Mach Intell 2024); deep perturbation predictors fail to beat 'add the two single effects' (Ahlmann-Eltze et al., Nature Methods 2025); and pretraining performance plateaus at a fraction of current corpus sizes — no scaling law (DenAdel et al., Nature Methods 2026: 400 models, 6,400 experiments). Consequence: pat-1's learned layer is earned above a crossover whose location is an empirical fact about the data, not a belief about architecture — the perfect engine locates it by standing one-step-ahead comparison against its own auditable factor layer (prequential held-out log-loss; REQUESTS row 2026-08-26 asks the product to publish exactly this). At InSight's current scale — a K=8 streaming factorization whose tab gates on 24 questions fitted at a basis of 8, plus 8 of the viewer's own answers — the factor layer is the presumptive engine until the comparison is run: no cited source measures anything at this regime, in either direction, which is exactly why the standing comparison is the claim. Verification grade as pat-1: multi-index corroboration, journal pages egress-blocked, figures abstract/snippet-grade. Crossing note (2026-08-28, code-verified this run): the standing comparison this node calls for now has its instrument — the 2026-08-26 REQUESTS row was ruled worth-building and carried across the bridge as D325 (2026-08-27, the bridge's first crossing): the nightly fit publishes a prequential-online quality block on v2_patterns/loadings (newest day's pooled surprisal bits with basis, a ≤90-day pooled series, per-question daily means floored at n=8, and the verdict's required clause that it scores the fit, not the device Oracle's separate ridge solve), read first-hand in functions/src/patternsFit.ts and functions/src/patterns.ts. The crossover is thereby measurable in principle; this node's path to 'measured' waits on the scorecard's VALUES becoming readable from main — the map lane's 2026-08-28 REQUESTS row asks exactly that, on behalf of this lane and cen-2 too, and is seconded rather than duplicated.

nodes.claim: Distillation from learned representation to auditable factors is demonstrated technology whose faithfulness is unsolved — the perfect audit layer is a psychometric instrument with measured faithfulness, not an explanation extracted after the fact.
nodes.detail: The channel exists at every scale tried: a teacher network distills into a soft decision tree that generalizes better than the same tree trained on raw data (Frosst & Hinton 2017, 96.76% MNIST vs 94.45% for the same tree trained on true targets, snippet-grade); concept bottleneck models carry near-parity task accuracy while supporting test-time intervention on a named concept (Koh et al., ICML 2020); sparse autoencoders decompose a production LLM's representations into features that are individually interpretable and causally steerable — clamping one feature rewrites the model's self-concept (Bricken et al. 2023; Templeton et al. 2024; independently Cunningham et al., ICLR 2024). But every documented failure mode attacks faithfulness, not capability, and they are the exact failure modes an InSight audit layer would inherit: concept leakage — learned concepts smuggle information beyond their definitions, natural mitigations do not fully work (Mahinpei et al. 2021); ungrounded concepts — the layer says 'beak colour' while the model used something else (Margeloiu et al. 2021); a measured tradeoff where making the label head stronger corrupts concept accuracy and intervenability (Havasi et al., NeurIPS 2022); dictionary pathology — the number of factors is chosen, not identified (feature splitting across a 512→131k width sweep, Bricken et al.; ~65% dead features at 34M scale, Templeton et al., snippet-grade), and SAE probes underperform plain logistic regression across 113 tasks in each regime on the mean across datasets (Kantamneni et al., ICML 2025); with Makelov et al. (arXiv:2405.08366) an early principled faithfulness evaluation — benchmarking learned dictionaries against supervised ground truth and finding legibility outruns causal control there too. Two consequences for the perfect engine. First, pat-2's 'distillation quality as a first-class metric' is the underserved gap, not a nicety — Templeton et al. themselves name the absence of rigorous faithfulness evaluation as a limitation; a program that PUBLISHES its distilled layer must hold it to a higher bar than the interpretability literature currently clears. Second, that bar already exists: psychometric factor/IRT models ship calibration, invariance testing, and inspectable item parameters as a mature apparatus (Embretson & Reise 2000) — the perfect audit layer is built as an IRT-grade instrument the learned layer must agree with out of sample, not as a post-hoc explanation of the learned layer. Verification grade as pat-1; three flags kept honest: the Mahinpei soft-vs-hard-leakage direction is unresolved (not claimed here), Scaling Monosemanticity is cited by its canonical web URL not its purported arXiv mirror, and Makelov's venue year is unresolved (cited by arXiv id).

nodes.claim: The information budget is two-dimensional — persons and occasions-per-person — and the dimensions substitute only for population-level estimands: a person-specific coupling is bounded by that person's own occasions, which no crowd size can supply.
nodes.detail: Added 2026-08-28 as pat-4's second dimension. pat-4 budgets pairs by the paired count — the resource that first identifies a coupling and then sharpens it; within-person estimands (pat-3) add an orthogonal resource, occasions per person, and the substitution law between the two is itself measured. For population-average dynamic parameters N and T compensate: estimation performance rises with more persons at constant T and with more time points at constant N — named and mapped as the N/T compensation effect (Hecht & Zitzmann 2021, abstract-grade, in continuous-time modeling), and the DSEM simulation study built for exactly this question is REPORTED to find large-N/small-T outperforming small-N/large-T — an ordering that circulates secondary-grade via citing papers (McNeish 2019, 'Two-Level Dynamic Structural Equation Models with Small Samples', SEM 26(6):948–966, DOI 10.1080/10705511.2019.1578657, is the reachable carrier), whose specific numbers DISAGREE across carriers (N=200/T=10 vs N=200/T=100 vs T≤20 at N≥250) — so the ordering is carried and the number is not (Schultzberg & Muthén 2018 — design verified abstract-grade: two-level AR(1) models, Bayesian in Mplus 8, varying model complexity, number of subjects and number of time points; its headline figures stay flagged for a primary read and nothing here leans on them). For PERSON-SPECIFIC estimands the compensation fails structurally: another person's stream carries no information about this person's dynamics beyond a group prior — which is precisely what the group-pooled machinery at pat-10 (GIMME; fissioned from pat-3, 2026-09-01) formalizes as a starting structure, partial relief rather than substitution — and the feasibility study for idiographic networks prices the demand upward, not downward: the ≥75-timepoints-for-6-nodes figure circulating as the field's floor is one the study's own simulation does not clear — sensitivity was LOW at the 75 and 100 timepoint conditions feasible in practice — and, sharpest, under short series the CORRECTLY SPECIFIED VAR(1) lost predictive accuracy to simpler models through overfitting (Mansueto et al. 2023, snippet-grade figures; the overfitting sentence corroborated this run from a single index paraphrase only, and is flagged as a named scout item for a primary read before anything leans further on it). If it holds at first hand, that result is this node's teeth: an engine built for a within-person estimand its data cannot pay for produces confidently wrong personalized couplings — a worse failure than level conflation, because it is personalized. Design consequence: when occasions are the binding resource, density is bought by design rather than volume — the measurement-burst design concentrates intensive occasions into repeated bursts precisely to fund within-person estimands over the long run (Nesselroade 1991, metadata-grade, an unread chapter cited as the design's origin; Sliwinski 2008, abstract-grade) — which for an InSight-shaped system means within-person coupling capacity concentrates where an axis repeats by nature (sensors, daily self-report), while the question axis buys occasions only by re-asking, under pat-5's retest discipline. Scope against db-8, drawn deliberately: db-8 owns the read side — which cells are publishable under the density budget, and sampling-design-as-meaning; this node is the estimand-side refinement of that density law — which ESTIMANDS are affordable at a given (N, T) allocation and what the marginal observation buys per dimension, the term cen-2's portfolio inherits through pat-4.

nodes.claim: Level conflation is an estimator property — not one more data fixes: where a construct's stability is at all trait-like, a level-blind cross-lagged estimator returns an uninterpretable amalgam of between- and within-person associations, with failure modes in the presence, predominance and sign of inferred influences.
nodes.detail: Fissioned from pat-3 2026-09-01 (central's 2026-08-28 question; go-7's budget argument); the evidence is the 2026-08-28 scout's, moved intact with its grades. Where a construct's stability is to any extent trait-like and time-invariant — the authors' own load-bearing conditional, kept here — the classical cross-lagged panel model fails to account for it, its lagged parameters then 'do not represent the actual within-person relationships over time', and the licensed errors are about the presence, predominance, and sign of causal influences — the three failure modes are the authors' own list (Hamaker, Kuiper & Grasman 2015, abstract-grade; the random-intercept fix they propose is what the field later named the RI-CLPM; no simulation is attributed to this paper). A level-blind cross-lagged panel estimator returns 'a weighted—and typically uninterpretable—amalgam of between- and within-person associations' (Berry & Willoughby 2017, abstract-grade, on the ARCL model specifically — the generalisation to level-blind engines at large is this lane's inference and marked so). Simulation shows both failure directions with the source's own asymmetry kept: spurious cross-lagged effects are very likely found where none exist, and real ones can sometimes be underestimated (Lucas 2023, abstract-grade), with CLPM bias under unmeasured stable confounding independently confirmed by simulation (Lüdtke & Robitzsch 2022, abstract-grade). The empirical sign-reversal instance (Dietvorst et al. 2018) lives at pat-3, whose estimand thesis it evidences; this node is the machinery half. This lane's inference, marked so: where Hamaker's conditional holds — the construct carries trait-like between-person variance — the conflation happens inside the estimator, and more persons do not discharge the problem; only level-aware estimation does (pat-10).
sources: Hamaker, Kuiper & Grasman, 'A critique of the cross-lagged panel model', Psychological Methods 20(1):102–116 (2015), DOI 10.1037/a0038889, PMID 25822208
Berry & Willoughby, 'On the practical interpretability of cross-lagged panel models: Rethinking a developmental workhorse', Child Development 88(4):1186–1206 (2017), DOI 10.1111/cdev.12660
Lucas, 'Why the cross-lagged panel model is almost never the right choice', Advances in Methods and Practices in Psychological Science 6(1):25152459231158378 (2023), DOI 10.1177/25152459231158378

Lüdtke & Robitzsch, 'A comparison of different approaches for estimating cross-lagged effects from a causal inference perspective', Structural Equation Modeling 29(6):888–907 (2022), DOI 10.1080/10705511.2022.2065278

nodes.claim: Native person-period machinery exists — two-level dynamic SEM, multilevel VAR's three separately-estimable networks (temporal within-person, contemporaneous within-person, between-person), group-pooled individual model recovery — so a level-blind engine conflates three objects, not two.
nodes.detail: Fissioned from pat-3 2026-09-01 (central's 2026-08-28 question; go-7's budget argument); the evidence is the 2026-08-28 scout's, moved intact with its grades. Two-level dynamic SEM carries person-specific dynamics under a between-person structural model, Bayesian, at intensive-longitudinal scale (Asparouhov, Hamaker & Muthén 2018; McNeish & Hamaker 2020 as the operational primer). Multilevel VAR separates coupling structure into THREE separately-estimable networks — temporal within-person, contemporaneous within-person, between-person — that need not agree (Epskamp, Waldorp, Mõttus & Borsboom 2018, abstract-grade for the three-network decomposition; mlVAR/graphicalVAR), so the conflation pat-9 describes folds three objects, not two — and the decomposition supplies the audit layer's level-label set (this lane's inference, marked so: between · within-temporal · within-contemporaneous is the type system pat-3's level-labeled publication rule carries). Group-pooled model search recovers individual-level directed dynamic models by using the replicated group skeleton as each person's starting structure (Gates & Molenaar 2012 — the qualitative recovery result; the circulating 97%/95% presence/direction figures are snippet-grade with unverified conditions and are not relied on) — which is also the partial relief pat-8 names: a group prior over person-specific structure, never a substitute for that person's own occasions. All of this machinery is defined over person-period records and none of it can be run on person-aggregates (this lane's inference from the methods' own definitions, marked so) — the operational content of pat-3's native-record consequence.
sources: Asparouhov, Hamaker & Muthén, 'Dynamic structural equation models', Structural Equation Modeling 25(3):359–388 (2018), DOI 10.1080/10705511.2017.1406803

McNeish & Hamaker, 'A primer on two-level dynamic structural equation models for intensive longitudinal data in Mplus', Psychological Methods 25(5):610–635 (2020), DOI 10.1037/met0000250, PMID 31855015
Epskamp, Waldorp, Mõttus & Borsboom, 'The Gaussian graphical model in cross-sectional and time-series data', Multivariate Behavioral Research 53(4):453–480 (2018), DOI 10.1080/00273171.2018.1454823

Gates & Molenaar, 'Group search algorithm recovers effective connectivity maps for individuals in homogeneous and heterogeneous samples', NeuroImage 63(1):310–319 (2012), DOI 10.1016/j.neuroimage.2012.06.026 (the GIMME paper — GIMME is the algorithm's name, not the title)

nodes.claim: The level separation is not free or automatic: centering and detrending policy change the disaggregated answer, person-specific reliability is its own estimand, and the random-intercept adjustment is parametric — with time-varying confounding a standing residual this node does not claim away.
nodes.detail: Fissioned from pat-3 2026-09-01 (central's 2026-08-28 question; go-7's budget argument); the evidence is the 2026-08-28 scout's, moved intact with its grades. Three costs, each its own literature. (1) Centering and detrending policy change the disaggregated answer — three centering by four detrending choices, examined in the same journal issue as the CLPM critique (Wang & Maxwell 2015); this lane's gloss, marked so: the within/between split is an analytic decision, not a button. (2) Multilevel autoregressive practice routinely assumes perfect reliability, and person-specific reliability is its own estimand (Schuurman & Hamaker 2019) — and, this lane's inference marked so: an occasion is worth what the state instrument's reliability says it is, the engine-side analogue of the body lane's instrument-validity boundary (bod-7 — an analogy between a reliability boundary and a validity boundary, not a shared result). (3) The random-intercept adjustment is parametric, not the design-based fixed-effects difference-out — the latent approaches 'strongly depend on the specific parametric assumptions' (Lüdtke & Robitzsch 2022, abstract-grade) — and even the design-based guarantee covers time-invariant confounding only, so time-varying confounding (a life event moves sleep, mood and answering at once) remains a standing residual this node does not claim away. Consequence for the engine, this lane's inference and marked so: the level split is itself a modeled, versioned analytic policy, published beside the coupling like any other basis declaration (pat-2; map-6's declared-basis rule) — because two correct engines with different centering policies publish different within-person numbers from the same records, a reader who cannot see the policy cannot recompute the number.
sources: Wang & Maxwell, 'On disaggregating between-person and within-person effects with longitudinal data using multilevel models', Psychological Methods 20(1):63–83 (2015), DOI 10.1037/met0000030, PMID 25822206
Schuurman & Hamaker, 'Measurement error and person-specific reliability in multilevel autoregressive modeling', Psychological Methods 24(1):70–91 (2019), DOI 10.1037/met0000188

nodes.claim: Pairing is a design variable, not a given: the conserved answer budget is allocated by planned-missing design — matrix sampling for population estimands, the two-method design for expensive axes — under full-information estimation, so the marginal value of one more paired person on a declared target coupling is the quantity a design criterion would have to compute — information per cost, not taste; the design buys precision-not-bias only for the missingness the engine itself assigns, pays in efficiency where the coupling is manifest rather than latent, and buys a model-free coupling only by co-service.
nodes.detail: pat-4's constructive half (2026-09-02): if pairing identifies a coupling, the engine designs it. FOUR PIECES. (1) Matrix sampling is the operating principle under a conserved budget: a pool no person finishes, forms to random subgroups (Shoemaker 1973), population characteristics estimated with plausible values where nobody answers enough to be scored (Mislevy, Beaton, Kaplan & Sheehan 1992; Mislevy 1991 — tst-7's machinery, here as design; PISA/TIMSS, González & Rutkowski 2010). (2) Designer-assigned missingness is MCAR by construction, so under full-information estimation (Arbuckle 1996; Little & Rubin; Enders) it costs precision, not bias (Rioux et al. 2020; Graham et al. 2006). (3) The two-method design (gold standard on a subset, a cheap same-construct indicator on everyone) beats a SAME-COST complete-cases design on standard errors and effective n, most where the cost differential is large and the effect small (Graham et al. 2006, abstract-grade), given random assignment — a genome or sensor against the daily stream. (4) Design is a decision problem solved by maximising expected utility (Chaloner & Verdinelli 1995, abstract-grade); cost inside the utility and criteria on the Fisher information matrix are textbook optimal-design practice (Atkinson, Donev & Tobias 2007; Berger & Wong 2009 — index-grade, content not read). TWO BOUNDARIES. Planned missingness is not efficiency-neutral: at equal data points a reduced-n complete design can win, manifest-variable regression coefficients markedly so, latent models being where the design pays (Rhemtulla, Savalei & Little 2016, abstract-grade) — the advantage is claimed cost-matched only. And two items never served together carry no MODEL-FREE information about their own coupling — nonparametrically, pat-4's Fréchet case; a latent model with an everyone-block identifies it through shared loadings, which is why the design pays for latent and loses for manifest — so for an engine whose product IS couplings co-service buys the model-free coupling: the everyone-block is que-1's spine, a tail–tail coupling model-free only at its co-service rate (this lane's inference, marked; que-5 agrees: spine items raise no coupling's n). The MCAR guarantee covers only what the engine assigns — genome upload or sensor wear is self-selected, MAR at best: pat-5's and db-8's territory. SYNTHESIS, this lane's own, marked — no verified source computes it for a coupling matrix: one more paired person's marginal value is expected information gain on the declared target coupling per cost, defined only against a declared model and target, which cen-2's currency supplies. Verification: full texts egress-blocked; sources search-index-corroborated, graded per string.
